evidence.note: ManifestContext.Satisfies matches spec section 6 of docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.8.3-sharded-review-results.md clause for clause: reasons subset of {DIFF_TRUNCATED, LARGE_DIFF}, Present, ShardCount>0, ShardsCovered==ShardCount, (ShardCount==1 or CrossShard), Verdict==PASS. No drift found.

Checked the truncation downgrade for a hole: staged/worktree truncation raises LOCAL_DIFF_TRUNCATED, which is not in shardSatisfiableReasons, so sharded stays false and the 'Diff context was truncated' finding keeps blocking for local content that no shard pack carries. Same for UNTRACKED_OMITTED/UNTRACKED_TRUNCATED/DIFF_OVERSIZE. The downgrade is sound.

untrackedExcerpt writes '--- <rel>' then prefixes EVERY content line with '+', so addedUntrackedLines' claim that content can never begin a line with '--- ' is verified against the producer; a file cannot move the lint scope by naming a path of its own.

addedSourceLines: '+++ ' is honoured as metadata only while inHeader (before the first @@), and a bare '+++' in a hunk body is now kept, so an added source line starting with '++' is no longer walked past the lints. Verified /dev/null guard on deletions and that renames/quoted paths resolve through diffHeaderPath's LastIndex on ' b/' and ' "b/'.

Verified the PASS_ADVISORY worry is a non-issue: the aggregate verdict is PASS unless blockers exist (verdictBlocks covers only NEEDS_REVISION/ESCALATED), so a shard result of PASS_ADVISORY still clears Satisfies' Verdict==PASS. Plan-hash freshness is enforced at ingestion (manifest.go:189), which is why Satisfies need not re-check PlanHash.

The context-risk fingerprint change from reason-bearing to 'architecture:context-risk' has the section 8 migration behind it: legacyContextRiskPrefixes covers all three scopes (architecture:, pr:architecture:, epic:) and supersedeLegacyContextRisk marks old rows 'superseded' with an empty fixedInRunId, so prior open rows neither block nor read as fixes.

Tests exist for every new production path in this shard. Ran go test ./internal/reviewers/: ok, 97.0% unit-only, floor for internal/reviewers is 97.7 combined (tests/coverage-floor.txt:19). Per-function coverage is 100% for Satisfies, RunTaskDone, manifestFound, contextRiskCoveredFound, addedLines, addedSourceLines, addedUntrackedLines, lintable, diffHeaderPath, postImagePath.

Walked the wait loop for the empty-RUNS case by hand: printf of an empty RUNS yields one blank line, so TOTAL (grep -c .) is 0 while PENDING (grep -vc completed) is 1, and the TOTAL>0 guard correctly reads that as 'not ready' rather than 'all done'. The || true guards keep the step alive under bash -e, and PIPESTATUS[0] is read while set +e is in force.

Action pinning matches the repository convention: actions/setup-python is pinned to a commit SHA with a version comment, exactly as .github/workflows/test.yml pins checkout, setup-go, setup-node and golangci-lint-action.

findings.note: Undocumented narrowing of the deterministic lint scope. lintable() excludes every path ending .md/.markdown anywhere in the tree and everything under docs/, so an added TODO/FIXME or an unsafe dynamic-evaluation call in any Markdown file is now invisible to the gate. The change is deliberate, commented, and tested, but spec section 6 says only that 'the lints then run over the union added lines' and never states the prose carve-out; the spec should record the blind spot it accepts.

evidence.note: lintable returns false for any .md/.markdown suffix and any docs/ prefix, matched case-insensitively.
Spec section 6 describes the satisfied path as running 'the lints then ... over the union added lines' with no mention of a documentation exclusion.

findings.note: manifestFound returns the empty string whenever ShardCount == 0, which also suppresses the 'no shard review results were ingested' note and the manifest verdict it was added to surface. A run where a manifest is Present but reports zero shards therefore produces a blocking context-risk finding whose Found text says nothing about why the manifest failed to satisfy it, which is the diagnostic spec section 6's unsatisfied path asks for.

evidence.note: Early return on manifest.ShardCount == 0 happens before the Present check that would emit 'no shard review results were ingested'.

findings.note: Test gap on the single-shard satisfied plan. boolString is the only new function below 100% statement coverage (66.7%): its false branch is unreached, meaning no test exercises contextRiskCoveredFound for a satisfied plan with ShardCount == 1 and CrossShard == false — a combination Satisfies explicitly permits, so the advisory text for the commonest small-plan case is unverified.

evidence.note: go tool cover -func reports boolString at 66.7%; every other new function in this file reports 100.0%.

findings.note: gtg.yml requests statuses: read but never reads commit statuses; the wait loop polls /check-runs only. Two consequences: an unused permission in the grant, and a legacy commit status (a non-check-run reporter) is neither waited for nor excluded by name, so gtg can be started before it settles.

evidence.note: permissions grants statuses: read; the only API calls in the file are repos/*/pulls/* and repos/*/commits/*/check-runs.

findings.note: Timeout budget is tight rather than wrong: timeout-minutes is 30 while the documented wait budget alone is 132 * 10s = 22 minutes, leaving roughly 8 minutes for pip install, the API round trips and gtg itself. If CI ever runs to its own 20-minute ceiling the job can be killed by the runner rather than reporting the warning the wait loop was written to emit.

evidence.note: timeout-minutes: 30 at job level against a 22-minute in-step retry budget plus install and gtg execution.
